title: The perfect music streaming app does not exist
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: The Nothing Phone 2A
recommendations.blurb: I t has been a long time since I was this excited about a cheap smartphone. It doesn’t work on every network in the US, but a $350 phone that looks good and makes mostly reasonable compromises ? More of this, please.

recommendations.name: Last Week Tonight ’s Boeing segment
recommendations.blurb: Telling you to watch John Oliver is not groundbreaking information, I know. But this is a really good one! And it tells a story about how companies and products change that will sound like an awful lot of the tech industry.

recommendations.name: The Logitech MX Brio
recommendations.blurb: This high-end $200 webcam might be two years too late to really be everywhere, but I’ve been looking for a webcam that is both good and simple for… forever and still haven’t found it. Logitech always nails simple, and this one sounds like it might really be good .

recommendations.name: The Gentlemen
recommendations.blurb: A high-budget, high-concept Netflix show about fancy people and drugs based on a deeply silly action movie? I’d watch every second of this even if it was awful — but based on the early feedback, it’s not awful at all .

recommendations.name: MyMind
recommendations.blurb: This has long been one of my favorite apps: it’s like a personal Pinterest, a place to keep all the stuff you care about and like and want to remember.

recommendations.name: CleanMyPhone
recommendations.blurb: MacPaw makes some of my favorite device cleanup devices (CleanMyMac and CleanMyPC have saved me a million times), and I’m already digging this as a way to clean up my iPhone’s camera roll. The app’s expensive ($24.99 a year), but you can get a lot done in the three-day free trial… just saying.

recommendations.name: The BEST remote control was made in 2005
recommendations.blurb: “ The BEST remote control was made in 2005 .” I will never stop wanting great universal remotes to be a thing. Never ever ever. This very funny 16-minute video about the Harmony 880, one of the all-time greats, had me eBay shopping for one of my own.

recommendations.name: The M3 MacBook Air
recommendations.blurb: I will always miss the wedge design, but I’m already beginning to talk myself into upgrading — the new Air’s battery and performance both sound ridiculous, and I’m extremely into that midnight color. I don’t need a new computer, I don’t need a new computer, I don’t need a new computer.

recommendations.name: The Rivian R3
recommendations.blurb: The new R2 also looks good — cheaper, glove compartments, two scroll wheels?! — and is definitely coming sooner . But I’m really into the R3, which is smaller and sportier and gives me vintage Land Rover vibes in a way I very much enjoy .

recommendations.name: Maybe all the music services are bad? I heard from a lot of what I’d call “Begru
recommendations.blurb: dging Music Streamers” who hate the interface and the lack of high-quality audio in their app but feel stuck for one reason or another. (Family plans keep us all locked in, it seems.)

recommendations.name: Apple Music wins on interface
recommendations.blurb: Almost everyone who told me they liked Apple Music told me they liked its tools for managing playlists and libraries. If you’re the organizing type, there’s no better music app.

recommendations.name: But Spotify wins on recommendations
recommendations.blurb: Turns out, the same thing keeps you all hooked on Spotify that has me there, too: personalized playlists like Release Radar and the Daily Mixes, along with being able to see what your friends are listening to.

recommendations.name: Spotify is also everywhere
recommendations.blurb: It’s integrated into Bluetooth speakers, Sonos speakers, lots of car interfaces, fitness trackers, voice assistants, and practically everything else. That was important to a lot of folks — your music service should be available everywhere you want music, and Spotify has that pretty much covered.

recommendations.name: YouTube wins by being YouTube
recommendations.blurb: I really thought you’d all make fun of me for spending a billion dollars a month on YouTube Premium, but it turns out, I’m not alone! YouTube Music is kind of a meh app, but it’s included, and the overall YouTube corpus of music is just unbeatable.

recommendations.name: Plexamp
recommendations.blurb: Tidal is still kicking. I honestly think every single Tidal user emailed me this week to remind me that Tidal is good. I believe you! One person, Marcus, said they Plexamp to stream both Tidal and their local music collection, which is a pretty good trick.

recommendations.name: An iPhone 12 Mini
recommendations.blurb: The phone: An iPhone 12 Mini.

recommendations.name: Pedro Páramo
recommendations.blurb: Right now, I’m reading the new translation (by Douglas Weatherford) of Pedro Páramo , and I’ve been astonished at how much better I like it than the previous version I read. I’ve kind of been reading it more slowly than I usually read books because I don’t want it to end.

recommendations.name: One says JOYROOM on it
recommendations.blurb: Two clutch MagSafe mounts for the bathroom: one for next to the mirror and one for the shower. One says JOYROOM on it , which is hilarious in the context of a bathroom, but if you want to listen to a pod in the shower, it’s unbeatable.

recommendations.name: Peak Design mount
recommendations.blurb: Two clutch MagSafe mounts for the bathroom: one for next to the mirror and one for the shower. One says JOYROOM on it , which is hilarious in the context of a bathroom, but if you want to listen to a pod in the shower, it’s unbeatable.

recommendations.name: No Return
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been addicted to the new game mode “ No Return ” in The Last of Us Part II . The goal is to survive a series of encounters involving an impressive number of maps, objectives, modifiers, and characters that can be randomly picked or manually chosen.

recommendations.name: this macro pad
recommendations.blurb: Missing the iPod click wheel? I bought this macro pad mostly to make it so that rotating the knob with one finger scrolls up and down.

recommendations.name: Rainbow Plant Life
recommendations.blurb: Listening to the smart kitchen Vergecast episode , I thought I’d share the meal planning service I use from Rainbow Plant Life . Since it does a lot of what was mentioned in that episode just without using cameras and sensors.

recommendations.name: newsmap.js
recommendations.blurb: Check out newsmap.js . It visualizes Google News in a helpful way.

recommendations.name: the best explainer video you can watch
recommendations.blurb: This is the best explainer video you can watch about AR smart glasses tech and why it is so difficult to make them look like regular glasses.

recommendations.name: Lorcana
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been getting into Disney’s trading card game Lorcana . It’s a neat, fun, and surprisingly easy-to-learn TCG that I just got my nine-year-old sister to start playing, and she loves it. I can see myself spending a lot of money on it.

recommendations.name: When Phones Were Fun
recommendations.blurb: I’ve been rewatching Michael Fisher’s “ When Phones Were Fun ” series on YouTube, a delightful dive into a much more interesting time in mobile.

recommendations.name: Tokyo Vice
recommendations.blurb: The new season of Tokyo Vice is fantastic! The first season was good enough, with some fun ‘fish out of water’ bits and a compelling Yakuza story but season two is really driving the shit out of the character development- especially the side characters. I love it.

recommendations.name: Fantastical
recommendations.blurb: Fell in love again with Fantastical . The free version is damn good. Great design and what makes me love it more than Amie or Notion Cal is the intelligent natural language input and ability to sync with Todoist .

recommendations.name: Todoist

recommendations.name: interview with Colin and Samir
recommendations.blurb: Jacob Collier is one of those people I’ve seen a million times on TikTok and YouTube — big wild hair and cool sweaters, always talking about some esoteric musical theory I don’t understand but nonetheless will watch him talk about for an hour — but I know almost nothing about him.
